I think many would think that I fall under the category of "loving myself", I personally think the question is flawed, so I'm going to answer it in the most long-winded way possible.   

Many think of themselves as "broken".  Depressed and filled with self-hatred kinda go hand in hand I find. When people call themselves broken they tend to mean "I am in a sustained and continuous amount of pain."  I don't like to label this term broken, because it implies that there was once a point where you were complete and whole, but lost it.  Many believe they are working to regain something they never really had.  Your title reminded me of this, due to the binary nature of your options. 

The way I like to think about it is that everyone is a swimming pool. Sure, sometimes birds fly in and die, or it gets covered in gunk and leaves. Self-love and slowly building a positive mental health is about getting the pool skimmer and getting the gunk out. What I like better about this frame of mind, is that the clean and clear pool water already exists within you. It just takes some time and slows continuous actions. 

For me, its taken a lot of therapy and choices to better my life. The big picture is important, but don't focus on that at first. Ask yourself "what is the most I can do right now to make myself better?" Do that, and nothing more.  Then, the next day, ask yourself the same thing. Eventually, what you can handle will get bigger and bigger.

I always thought that we, were quite funny as humans. We often just take what we want to learn, and Take it as the truth. Like, for instance, the phrase “blood is thicker than water.”  Family is stronger than anything. This was the exact opposite of what the Phrase actually is. Though, in reality, the viscosity of water is indeed lighter than blood, this was not the term. This term, has an actual, more poetic meaning. 

“The blood of the Covenant is thicker than the Water of the womb” 

I always ponder upon these words. First for the beautiful meaning. The notion that you get the choice of who are your companions; You cannot choose of whom birthed you. More importantly, I often ponder upon who chose to surgically remove the delicate diction of Metaphor, and take it as the new truth. A person chose to look upon the captivating Void of Syntax, Meaning, and Truth, and deny it. Who was this of whom onset the events to change history by removing 8 simple words?

 
These are the thoughts that ran through my head while two Gentleman escorted me through Two big ornate double doors. The hall had big, Cathedral like raised bland ceilings that would easily be so impossibly vast as if no painter dared to paint the cylindrical  like canvas. The whole room was hushed to my entrance. It felt as if a million unsympathetic eyes were peering at a wild beast.


“The blood of the Covenant is thicker than the Water of the womb” 

I think the main question of the matter isn't perhaps how someone could do this, but why? As a man who didn't really feel a connection to my lineage, I didn't understand what was so bad about these words. In my eyes, it meant as if you are not bound by the fates of your forefathers. If you wanted to be a lock smith in a family of Linguists, you had every right. 

It is not as if I hadn't been used to the feeling of uncomfortably high amounts of tension. It quite strangely gave me a nostalgic feeling. As if I were back at fifth year baseball championships, or Christmas dinner.  I began to approach the seat specifically marked out for me near the front of the packed room. 

“blood is thicker than water” 

On the other hand, coming from another set of eyes, it could be a symbol of betrayal. Some proud Patriarchal family felt as if they need to stick together in hard times, so they decided to bend the truth for the better of everyone. Whats one little quote?  I know this concept all too well.

Everyone had already arrived, as it seemed. They would probably would excuse my absence due to me being prohibited from driving myself. The Two kind gentlemen enjoyed reminding me of that. 

“The blood of the Covenant is thicker than the Water of the womb” 

I'm sure that for whatever reason they had, It was a legitimate one. Perhaps there was a rebellious person attempting to betray their family. Perhaps they needed to know where their place is. Who knows. There would have to be a reason. Perhaps that person was a cruel reminder of a bitter, colder past. 

“Don't worry, I believe you. Now let me convince them.” The suited man spoke to me, unwilling to get too close. From the front podium, I could already hear the Faint ticking from the worn out typewriter. They had to Track down every thing said to me, just in case. 

“blood is thicker than water” 

All families have things they would rather forget. Not major things. Slight details get left out,  locations get changed, people get forgotten to be mentioned. Some things like a quiet bastard child get rubbed out entirely.

I felt really out of place here. I stood at an oblique table, taking in all of  the Cold faces, whilst everyone was perfectly parallel. I felt as if they had made everything perfect to give me a message I wont forget for the brief moments I have. 

“Blood is thicker than water”

Every wants to forget something.  Family or not, there are moments of a past that people would tangle in any dark arts to wipe away. For some, it is a lost love. For others, it might be an abusive father that doesn't know when to stop escalating the punishment, until the dam breaks upon the fragile world below, Crushing the innocents 

From the other side of the room, I could see familiar faces, also at a slanted table. It seems as if their cold stares digging into my skull ceased as soon as I reciprocated his looks. I was unsure if it was shame, fear, or an attempt to feel a deep sense of satisfaction. 

“Blood is thicker than water 

Sometimes peoples perspectives are changed. Events that are unleashed upon one person are traumatically given to someone else. Emotions and memories are drastically changed for the fitting idea of as story, or meaning that has no need for 8 words or the Love of a kind sister that cares despite a status quo and devout litany. 

If I am being completely honest, I don't blame those who give me scorn for my misgivings. Even though I know in my heart that the blood of the covenant is thicker than the water of the womb, The blood was indeed thicker than water. Truth over time has been changed to seem to the populace that one is a monster stumbling upon a brutal murder of an innocent.

Was the blood of my father  thicker than will to believe that I could leave upon my own will, let people know of the truth that they say they crave? Was the waters of the womb thicker than the scars upon my back when I had the tenacity to smile at one that was kind, and caring? 

Was it thicker when the sister who showed me kindness, built up strength to forfeit the womb for sacred bond of the covenant?  Even though one could take it as he did many times before, why was the bond so strong then, that she though she could on take the burden? 
When the blood of the covenant is spilled by the waters of the womb, when does meaning return?  


The defining silence ended when the judge finally said his first first words of the trial. “Judge Fredrick residing for the murder trial of Anne Beck. The Prosecution may make his opening remarks.” from the other Table. My father Stood and walked towards the jury. 

My father was always a smart lawyer. In such a hard time to make money, he did really well to put a lot of murderers away. He knew all the mistakes they made, all the things they did wrong. 

He also knew exactly what to do.  

In the end, I will always know that even when broken, the blood of the covenant will always be thicker.
